transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-10 16:00 UTC — Duration 48m — Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Aaron (Pelotonix CTO), Maya S (Pelotonix ML Eng), Diego (Pelotonix Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros then we'll run through the self-serve path and how long to expect first call.
[00:22] Aaron: Thanks, yeah we want something that gets our team to a realistic prototype in a few days, not weeks. Main constraints: PII-ish logs in the payloads, latency sub-200ms p95 for short prompts, and cost sensitivity.
[00:37] Liam: Cool, totally — so the usual flow we recommend is signup, org provisioning, free credits for pilot, quickstart with SDK, and then optional dedicated pilot if you need predictability. For Pelotonix I'd ask about your traffic pattern — bursty or steady?
[00:52] Aaron: Bursty, peaks during business hours — maybe 300 rps for short bursts, baseline like 10 to 20.
[01:05] Diego: And on security, we need KMS + SSO, and audit logs kept for a year. Also need to know whether we can keep inference inside our VPC eventually.
[01:18] Maya (AE): Yep, we have a Private offering — VPC or on-prem — that plugs into your KMS and can ship audit logs. For the quickstart, though, most teams start hosted to validate quality and integration.
[01:33] Maya S: How fast is first real call? Like from signup to our app making a token-level inference call?
[01:38] Liam: If you follow our playbook, you can be at first call in under 2 hours: create org, accept invite, install SDK, run sample prompt. Realistically, with IAM approvals and SSO flows it can be a day. But we'll provision credits and a short checklist to hit that target.
[01:58] Aaron: Ok, and about data retention — if we use hosted, do you redact logs or can we opt out?
[02:05] Maya: Hosted stores minimal request logs for billing and debugging; you can toggle log retention and opt-out of storing payloads. For enterprise we do dedicated/private where logs stay in your environment and we ship a control-plane-only integration.
[02:20] Diego: Cost — we need to understand token pricing and ways to optimize. Any tricks?
[02:27] Liam: Sure — batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variants. For quickstart we'll suggest a lower-cost model family to validate correctness, then run a small benchmark comparing latency/cost across model variants. Also we provide a Optimize report with recommendations.
[02:45] Aaron: Do you have any pre-baked benchmarking scripts? We want to simulate 300 rps bursts.
[02:51] Liam: Yes — I'll share a runbook: k6 + our SDK examples and a script that emulates sequence-length distributions. We'll set up a benchmark window where we reserve capacity if you want to avoid noisy neighbors.
[03:06] Maya S: What's the deal with KV cache? We use long chat contexts sometimes and need fast turn-taking.
[03:11] Liam: Our runtime supports KV cache and automatic prefix caching — sometimes the transcript shows it as K-V cash, ha — but in short, we keep the KV cache warm and reuse it for low-latency context. For hosted quickstart you're fine; dedicated gives stricter latency SLOs.
[03:28] Aaron: Security docs — can we get a SOC2 summary and details on encryption in transit and at rest?
[03:33] Maya: Absolutely — we'll send SOC2, ISO snapshot, and the KMS integration guide. If you need HSM-level controls, Private can support customer-managed HSMs in the VPC option.
[03:47] Diego: Who typically owns the pilot internally? Product or infra?
[03:51] Aaron: Usually infra for security and product for acceptance.
[03:55] Maya (AE): Good — we recommend a two-week micro-pilot: week 1 integration + correctness, week 2 load/latency benchmarks and cost analysis. Success criteria: functional parity on prompts (>=95% pass rate on eval set), and p95 latency <200ms for short calls, cost per 1k tokens within your target.
[04:18] Aaron: Sounds reasonable. For the eval set — we can share 200 prompts, average 64 tokens.
[04:25] Maya S: We'll provide that by Tuesday.
[04:28] Liam: Great. For the quickstart I'll run you through the exact commands now — sample cURL and node/python SDK snippets — then we'll provision credits.
[04:36] Liam: (screen-share note) Example: POST /v1/generate with X-API-Key header, model:redwood-alpha, temperature 0.0, max_tokens 128. You might see names in the docs like redwood-alpha but in the hosted catalog you'll pick the recommended variant.
[04:55] Diego: Any gotchas with CORS or browser usage?
[04:58] Maya: We recommend keeping secret keys server-side; for demos you can use ephemeral keys via our SDK. We'll add a sample reverse-proxy pattern to the runbook.
[05:10] Aaron: Do you do rate limits per token or per request?
[05:13] Liam: We have both. Quotas default per-org and per-key; during the pilot we'll relax limits for your benchmark window or provision reserved capacity.
[05:23] Maya S: If we like hosted but later need VPC, how painful is migration?
[05:28] Maya: We built the API to be compatible across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — same endpoints and SDKs. Migration is mostly about networking and KMS, not changing app code. Some tuning for quantized variants may be needed.
[05:42] Diego: Ok great. For the next steps can you send the quickstart checklist and the benchmark script?
[05:47] Maya: Yes — we'll send both plus the security artifacts. Also we'll provision $3k in credits up front.
[05:55] Aaron: That should cover our initial runs. After the benchmark we'll decide if we need a Dedicated pool.
[06:01] Liam: One more note: if you want extremely low jitter we can reserve a small Dedicated pool for the benchmark for a day; costs are predictable and we'll give a back-of-envelope.
[06:12] Aaron: Good to know. Anything else?
[06:14] Diego: No, that's it from product.
[06:16] Maya S: Nope, thanks.
[06:18] Maya (AE): I'll recap — Mia? (laugh) — recap: Redwood will: 1) provision org and $3k credits, 2) share quickstart runbook and benchmark scripts, 3) send SOC2/KMS notes. Pelotonix will: 1) share prompts and QPS details, 2) confirm benchmark window. We'll schedule the 2hr benchmark next week.
[06:43] Aaron: Thanks everyone.
[06:45] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with links.

Meeting end.
